tasks.subject: Task 1: Part 1 follow-ups (M1, M5, M6, M9, done-spec steps)
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The five edges that the queue runner makes reachable are closed: a plan readable after its worktree is gone, `run` refusing beside an unfinished spec, a pump before the drain, metrics steps that never park, and `engine resume` reconciling the open steps of a finished spec.

**Files:**
- Modify: `engine/lib/engine/core.js`, `engine/lib/engine/cli.js`, `engine/lib/engine/steps.js`
- Test: `engine/test/engine_core.test.js`, `engine/test/engine_cli.test.js`, `engine/test/engine_resume.test.js`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] M1: when `spec.worktree` no longer exists on disk, the core reads the plan (`plan(spec)`), the spec file and git state from `repo`. A `merge` spec whose worktree was removed and whose row is still `integrating` resumes to `done` without `engine_error`.
- [ ] M5: `engine run B` exits 1 with `engine: run: <A> is unfinished (<state>): use engine resume` and inserts nothing when the database holds a spec A that is not `done`. A spec in `awaiting_you` that already has an outcome (Task 8's end-of-queue failure) does not count as unfinished.
- [ ] M6: `tick()` calls `pumpAll()` before `drainAll()`. A test leaves an input event with none of its commands applied, inserts a worker inbox row, runs one tick, and finds the input's command events before the row's `inbox_worker` event (by seq).
- [ ] M9: the core runs `metrics start` itself, as the `metrics_start:<spec>` step, when a spec with a batch starts (before `spec_started` is written), and `cli.js` `cmdRun` no longer does. On `resume()`, a step of one of the six measurement and notice kinds of Global Constraints left at `intent` never parks: check `done` marks it done; `not_done` runs `metrics start` again for `metrics_start` and leaves the other kinds to their owner; `unknown` marks it `failed` with a `step_failed` event.
- [ ] Done-spec steps: `engine resume` with every spec `done` and a `close_window` row at `intent` starts the core, reconciles, runs one tick and exits 0 with `reconciled 1 step(s)`; the row ends `done`; with no row at `intent` it still prints `nothing to resume`.
- [ ] The two part 1 tests that tolerated a lost metrics start (`engine_resume.test.js`, titles starting "kill between spec_added" and "kill between step_intent and step_done of the metrics start") are tightened: after the resume exactly one `metrics start` call is in the stub's log, with the stub answering `metrics has start` by exit 1 until the start ran.
- [ ] Each guard test names its mutation in a comment.

**Verify:** `cd engine && node --test test/engine_core.test.js test/engine_cli.test.js test/engine_resume.test.js`

**Steps:**
- [ ] Read lines 255 to 264 of `docs/superpowers/ledgers/2026-11-23-pcee-engine-part-1/progress.md` (the final review's rulings and the `close_window` ruling). The findings M1, M5, M6 and M9 are restated in the criteria above; the code they name is `core.js` `plan()`, `tick()`, `resume()` and `cli.js` `cmdRun`, `cmdResume`.
- [ ] Write the failing tests first, one per criterion. Mutations to name: M1 "always use `spec.worktree`" → the removed-worktree test fails; M5 "drop the unfinished check" → `run B` inserts B; M6 "move `pumpAll()` after `drainAll()`" → the seq order test fails; M9 "park on unknown" → the metrics step test finds an open wait; done-spec "return before starting the core" → the row stays `intent`.
- [ ] M1: add one helper in `core.js` (`const wtOf = (spec) => (spec.worktree && fs.existsSync(spec.worktree) ? spec.worktree : repo)`) and use it at every `spec.worktree || repo`.
- [ ] M9: move the `metrics start` call out of `cmdRun` into a core function `metricsStart(spec)` that wraps the existing argv (`["metrics", "start", spec.id, "--batch", spec.batch, "--worktree", spec.worktree]`, cwd `repo`) in `steps.run` and swallows its error after the `step_failed` event; call it in `startQueued` before the `spec_started` emit, and from `resume()` for a `metrics_start` row the check answers `not_done`. In `resume()`, split `rec.park`: rows of the six kinds are marked failed, never parked. Add to `steps.js` `CHECKS.metrics_ask`, `CHECKS.artifact`, `CHECKS.awake_off` and `CHECKS.registry_report`, each `() => "unknown"` (Tasks 4 and 9 write those steps).
- [ ] Done-spec: in `cmdResume`, when no spec is open, count `steps` rows at `intent`; with any, start the core, `await eng.resume()`, `await eng.tick()`, print the count, stop.
- [ ] Run the Verify command: all pass. Run `cd engine && npm test`: no other suite regressed. Commit `fix(engine): part 1 follow-ups before the queue runner`.

tasks.subject: Task 2: claude-tmux reports model and usage limits (I5)
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A worker whose pane shows Claude's limit message produces a `status` event with state `usage_limit` or `model_limit`, so the core's existing handling (a `usage_reset` timer; one rerun on Opus) runs with real workers.

**Files:**
- Modify: `engine/lib/engine/backend/claude_tmux.js`, `engine/test/fixtures/engine/fake-worker.js`
- Test: `engine/test/engine_backend.test.js`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] In `poll()`, for each live handle whose latest agent-status state is `ready` or that has no record yet, the backend captures the pane's last 40 lines (`capture-pane -p -J -S -40`) and matches `/You've hit your (.+?) limit/`. Group 1 one of `5-hour`, `weekly`, `session` → one `status` event with `state: "usage_limit"`; any other text → `state: "model_limit"`. The event is emitted once per handle and carries `updatedAt` (the poll's time in seconds), `tool: null`, `lastToolAt: null`, `turnStartedAt: null`.
- [ ] A handle whose state is `busy` is not captured (a test counts the `capture-pane` calls through the logging tmux wrapper the suite already uses).
- [ ] `fake-worker.js` gains modes `usage-limit` and `model-limit`: each prints its sentence (`You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 12:30am (America/New_York)`; `You've hit your Fable limit · resets 1pm (America/New_York)`), writes a `ready` status and no report.
- [ ] On the scratch tmux server, with `fake-worker.js` standing in for `claude`: mode `usage-limit` yields `usage_limit`, mode `model-limit` yields `model_limit`, mode `noreport` yields neither.
- [ ] Probe on record (run by the plan author, 2026-11-24, read-only over `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`, synthetic assistant lines containing "limit"): `You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 12:30am (America/New_York)` 16 times, `You've hit your weekly limit · resets …` 10 times, `You've hit your session limit · resets 5:30pm (America/New_York)` 2 times; no model-limit line was found (assumption A8). The test file quotes these three sentences as its fixtures and says where they came from.
- [ ] Mutation named: "match `/limit/` only" → the `noreport` case (whose pane prints `no limit here`) reports a limit.

**Verify:** `cd engine && node --test test/engine_backend.test.js`

**Steps:**
- [ ] Add the two modes to `fake-worker.js`, and make mode `noreport` print the line `no limit here` before it idles.
- [ ] Write the three scratch-server tests and the capture-count test; run: they fail (no limit state emitted).
- [ ] Implement in `poll()`: a `limitSent` flag on the entry; the capture runs only when `!e.limitSent` and the state is `ready` or unknown.
- [ ] Run the Verify command: all pass. Commit `fix(engine): claude-tmux reports model and usage limits`.

tasks.subject: Task 3: Schema additions, typed waits, ask defaults
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The database, the policy module and the report parser carry what sections 8a and 8b need, and an existing part 1 database opens without loss.

An answered row is written as given. `db.putRaw` writes without the check; `rebuild.js` replays with `putRaw`.
- [ ] `policy.js`: `POLICY_VERSION = 2`; `ASK_KINDS`; `ASK_DEFAULTS` equal to the Global Constraints table (a test compares all five rows, all three fields); `recommendationFor(kind, override)` returns the override when given, else the default, else throws `no recommendation for <kind>`; `loadConfig(repo).budget` is `{attempts: 60, tokens: 5000000}` overridden per key by `engine.json` `budget`; `policyHash(config)` is the sha256 of the raw `engine.json` text (or `{}`), a newline and `JSON.stringify(ASK_DEFAULTS)`, so a changed default changes the hash.

tasks.subject: Task 4: Typed ask through core, strategy and CLI (8a)
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Every parking site writes a kind and a recommendation, the recommendation is shown first wherever the question is shown, and each user answer records whether it followed the recommendation, in the `ruling` event and as one `ask` metrics line.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `core.park(spec, question, step, {kind, recommendation?, options?})` throws `park needs a kind` without one and fills the recommendation with `policy.recommendationFor`. Each of the first eleven rows of the Global Constraints park-site table has a test in `engine_ask.test.js` that reaches the site with the fake backend and reads the open wait's `kind` and `recommendation` (all three fields). The placeholder `kind: "cannot_tell"` Task 3 left in `park` is gone.
- [ ] The strategy's two `park` commands carry `kind` (and `recommendation` where the table gives one); the `architect_decision` event carries `recommend`, and the strategy copies it into its `park` command. The strategy stays pure (its frozen-input test still passes).
- [ ] `integrate.js` `parked(question, recommendation?)`: the two live-checkout parks pass the table's recommendation; the others pass none.
- [ ] The `awaiting_you` event's detail has `kind` and `recommendation`, and its `text` is `I recommend: <option> (<confidence>): <why> — <question> — answer with: tmux-ctl engine signal <spec> <options>`. `engine status --waiting` prints, per wait, `  I recommend: <option> (<confidence>): <why>` as the first line under the spec id, then the question, options, asked at and the answer command.
- [ ] On a user answer: the `signal` event carries `wait`, `kind` and `recommendation`; the user `ruling` event carries `kind`, `recommended` (the option), `answer` and `followed` (`answer === recommended`). Tests cover `followed: true` and `followed: false`.
- [ ] After the ruling, one command `metrics_ask` runs `tmux-ctl metrics append ask --json <json> [--batch <id>]` (cwd `repo`) as the step `metrics_ask:<wait id>` and writes one `ask_recorded` event with `{cause, idx}`. The JSON has exactly the keys `spec, batch, kind, recommended, confidence, answer, followed, asked_at, answered_at`, the two times as ISO-8601 UTC strings. A failing command leaves a failed step and the spec goes on (test with a stub `tmux-ctl` that exits 1). A wait closed by `worker_busy`, `job_ended` or `closed` writes no `ask` line.
- [ ] Replay: a test applies the `signal` input, deletes the `ask_recorded` event to imitate a crash after the step, pumps again, and counts one `metrics append ask` call in the stub's log. Mutation named: "run the command without `steps.run`" → two calls.

tasks.subject: Task 5: Per-spec budget (8b)
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Each spec has an attempts and a tokens budget: every dispatch reserves one attempt, every job end adds its tokens, a reached cap or an unmeasurable job parks the spec, and the spend is shown and recorded.

**Files:**
- Modify: `engine/lib/engine/core.js`, `engine/lib/engine/cli.js`, `engine/lib/engine/integrate.js`, `engine/lib/engine/backend/fake.js`, `engine/lib/engine/backend/claude_tmux.js`
- Create: `engine/test/engine_budget.test.js`
- Test: `engine/test/engine_backend.test.js`, `engine/test/engine_integrate.test.js`, `engine/test/engine_cli.test.js`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `engine run` accepts `--budget-attempts N --budget-tokens N` (positive integers, else exit 2); `addSpec` stores `budget_attempts` and `budget_tokens` from the flags, else from `config.budget`, with `spent_attempts` and `spent_tokens` 0.
- [ ] Before a dispatch of a job whose detail has no `reserved`: when `spent_attempts >= budget_attempts` or `spent_tokens >= budget_tokens`, the spec parks with the table's `core:budget:cap` row (question `budget reached: attempts a/A, tokens t/T`, options `approve|fail`) and nothing is dispatched. Otherwise one `budget_reserve` event (`job`, `attempt`) is written in the transaction that increments `spent_attempts` and sets `reserved: true` in the job's detail; then the dispatch runs.
- [ ] The cap recommendation follows assumption A6: `{approve, "extend by 50%", medium}` or `{fail, "the spec is looping", medium}`; both cases tested. `approve` raises each reached cap to `Math.ceil(cap * 1.5)` (one `budget_extended` event with `{cause, idx}`) and the job is dispatched; `fail` fails the spec with the note.
- [ ] Backend `usage` (Global Constraints). `fake`: a step `{tokens: N}` or `{tokens: null}` in the job's script sets its answer; a job without one answers `{tokens: 0}`. `claude-tmux`: finds `<projects root>/*/<session id>.jsonl` (root: `opts.transcriptRoot`, else `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, else `~/.claude/projects`) and sums `input_tokens + output_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` over assistant lines whose `message.usage` exists, whose `message.model` is not `<synthetic>`, whose `timestamp` is at or after `since`, counted once per `message.id`; no session id, no file or no such row → `{tokens: null, reason}`.
- [ ] Probe on record (plan author, 2026-11-24, one real transcript of this project): 540 assistant usage rows carry 310 distinct `message.id`s (one id up to 12 times), so the sum is taken once per id; the usage keys are `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, and each line has a top-level `timestamp`. A test feeds a transcript with one message id on three lines and expects it counted once. Mutation named: "drop the id dedupe" → that test fails.
- [ ] Real-state check (read-only): one test runs the `claude-tmux` usage reader over the newest transcript under the real `~/.claude/projects` and asserts an integer greater than 0, printing the file count it looked at; it is skipped with a printed reason when that directory is absent.
- [ ] At a job's end (`finishJob` and `failAttempt`; not a job that never started) the core calls `backend.usage(handle, {since: job.started_at})`; a backend without `usage` counts as `{tokens: null, reason: "the backend reports no usage"}`. The job row gets `tokens`, the spec row `spent_tokens += tokens || 0`, both in the transaction of the job's end event, whose detail has `tokens` and, when null, `tokens_missing`.
- [ ] A job end with `tokens: null` parks the spec with the table's `core:budget:unknown:<job>` row; `approve` goes on with the tokens left null. When another wait is already open the park is skipped (`park_skipped`) and the run goes on.
- [ ] A fake run whose scripted token counts cross the token cap parks before the next dispatch with the right recommendation (spec Testing additions).
- [ ] Kill between `budget_reserve` and the dispatch: a child-process run is killed by pid right after the `budget_reserve` event appears; `engine resume` reaches the same outcome, with one `dispatched` event for that job and `spent_attempts` equal to the number of `dispatched` events. Mutation named: "reserve again when the job is still pending" → the count is one too high.
- [ ] `engine status <spec>` prints `  attempts a/A · tokens t/T`, with ` (lower bound)` appended when an ended job of the spec has null tokens. `integrate.finalize` adds `--budget <json>` and `--engine-jobs <json>` to `metrics record` in the Global Constraints shape; the part 1 tests that pin that argv are updated.

**Verify:** `cd engine && node --test test/engine_budget.test.js test/engine_backend.test.js test/engine_integrate.test.js test/engine_cli.test.js`

**Steps:**
- [ ] Write `engine_budget.test.js` (reserve, both caps, both recommendations, extend, unknown cost, lower bound, the kill test with a tally line `<kill point> <ok|FAIL> <ms>` under the test's temp dir as part 1's resume suite does) and the backend usage tests. Run: they fail.
- [ ] `fake.js` and `claude_tmux.js`: `usage`. `core.js`: the reserve and cap check at the top of `dispatch()` after the usage-pause check; tokens in `finishJob` and `failAttempt` (when `endNeedsYou` also returns a `specs` row, merge the two into one row); the unknown-cost park appended last in `expand` for `job_done`, `job_failed` and `architect_decision`; `coreSignal` cases `budget:cap` → `[{type: "extend_budget"}]` and `budget:unknown` → `[]`; `apply` for `extend_budget`.
- [ ] `cli.js`: the two flags in `VALUE_FLAGS`, `cmdRun`, the status line. `integrate.js`: the two `metrics record` flags.
- [ ] Run the Verify command, then `cd engine && npm test`: all pass (part 1 suites keep passing because a scripted job without a tokens step counts 0). Commit `feat(engine): per-spec attempts and tokens budget`.

tasks.subject: Task 7: Queue runner: enqueue, start, done, gates, lines
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `engine enqueue`, `engine start` and `engine done` run a queue of engine-run, lead-run and gated specs in order, one spec at a time, and everything the lead must hear is a line in the lead-lines file.

**Constraints:**
- The contracts in Global Constraints (queue events, lead lines, assumptions A2 and A5) are fixed. No new spec state.
- CLI, each with `--project P` as today:
  - `engine enqueue <spec> --runner lead|engine --integration merge|mr|keep [--push] --batch <id> [--gate <id>] [--worktree <path>] [--budget-attempts N] [--budget-tokens N]` writes one inbox row (source `user`, kind `enqueue`, `source_id` `enqueue:<spec>@<batch>`) and prints `queued <spec> (<runner>)`. For runner `engine` it checks the plan as `engine run` does, in `--worktree` (default: the cwd's checkout); a spec the engine cannot run (no plan, no `.tasks.json`, a task without `verifyCommand`) is queued with runner `lead`, prints `engine: enqueue: <why>: queued for the lead`, and exits 0 (spec Error handling). Bad arguments exit 2; a spec already in `specs` exits 1.
  - `engine start [--preflight] [--here] [--backend claude-tmux|fake] [--script F]` resumes (section 9) and runs the queue loop in the foreground until the queue is finished; exit 0 then, 1 after `engine_error`. `--preflight` only checks and exits: 0 when the lock is free and there is a new `enqueue` row or a spec that is not `done`; 1 with one reason line otherwise. `--here` is accepted and ignored (Task 10's wrapper passes it).
  - `engine done <spec> --outcome <text>` writes one inbox row (kind `done`); exit 2 with `no lead turn open for <spec>` unless the spec is lead-run and `running`.
  - `engine status --unfinished` exits 0 and prints the spec ids when a queue is unfinished (a spec that is not `done`, not counting an `awaiting_you` spec that has an outcome, and no `queue_finished` event after the newest `spec_added`), else exits 1 and prints nothing.
- The turn: at most one spec is in `planning|running|final_review|integrating`. When none is, the next queued spec by position gets the turn. Runner `engine`: the plan is compiled first, and a plan that no longer compiles turns the spec into a lead-run one (`handed_to_lead`). Runner `lead`: with `--gate`, the gate is run first (`gate_result`; any exit but 0 completes the spec as `failed — gate <id>: <first output line>` and records it with `metrics record … --outcome failed` when it has a batch); then `lead_turn`, and the engine waits, ticking, for the `done` row. A lead-run spec never reaches the strategy.
- `lead.js` derives the lines from the events (Global Constraints) and is called by the queue loop after every tick; `engine run` does not call it. Its cursor is the last line's `seq` in the file; when that is greater than the database's highest seq (a new database), the file is renamed `<name>.old` and the cursor is 0.
- `engine run` and its part 1 tests keep working unchanged.

**Files:**
- Create: `engine/lib/engine/queue.js`, `engine/lib/engine/lead.js`, `engine/test/engine_queue.test.js`
- Modify: `engine/lib/engine/core.js`, `engine/lib/engine/cli.js`, `engine/test/engine_cli.test.js`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Queue runner test (spec Testing, "Queue runner"), child processes on the fake backend: three fixture specs enqueued as engine, lead and gated-lead whose gate stub exits 1. The run order is the queue order; the engine spec reaches `kept …`; the lead-run spec gets `lead_turn` and waits until `engine done <spec> --outcome "merged abc1234"` is run, then is `done` with that outcome; the gated spec is `failed — gate K9: <the stub's line>` with no `lead_turn`; `engine start` exits 0.
- [ ] The lead-lines file of that run holds `[Engine] your turn: <lead spec>` once, in seq order with the other lines; a second scenario's file holds each of `awaiting you`, `paused: usage limit until`, and `stopped:` (a user-gate task; a scripted `usage_limit` status; a stub that makes the core throw). A test that runs `lead.publish` twice finds no duplicate seq. Mutation named: "start the cursor at 0 on every call" → duplicates.
- [ ] A gate stub that exits 0 leads to `lead_turn`; one that exits 3 fails the spec like exit 1.
- [ ] `enqueue` twice for one spec and batch is one inbox row; `enqueue` writes no table but `inbox` (row counts of every other table before and after); a plan without a `verifyCommand` is queued for the lead with the stated line and gets `[Engine] your turn` at its turn.
- [ ] `engine done` for a spec that is not at a lead turn exits 2; `start --preflight` exits 1 while another engine holds the lock and 0 with a pending `enqueue` row; `status --unfinished` exits 0 mid-queue and 1 on an empty database.
- [ ] Kill and restart: `engine start` killed by pid while the lead-run spec waits, then `engine start` again: no second `lead_turn` event, no second `your turn` line, and `engine done` then completes the queue. `engine rebuild --check` exits 0 at the end of every scenario.
- [ ] A queue spec with a batch gets its `metrics start` through the core's `metrics_start` step (Task 1), counted once in the stub's log.
- [ ] Aged state: one in-process run with an injected clock leaves a lead turn open and moves the clock 25 hours on, across a day boundary, ticking: no timer fails or parks the lead-run spec, no second `lead_turn` is written, and `engine done` still completes it.
- [ ] Guard tests name their mutations.

tasks.subject: Task 8: Parked specs across the queue; end of the queue
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A parked spec gives the turn away, an answered one gets it back before the next queued spec, and at the end of the queue an unanswered one is completed as failed with its wait kept, so a later answer and `engine resume` finish it.

**Constraints:**
- One spec holds the turn (Task 7). A parked spec's answer that arrives while another spec holds the turn is stored on the wait at once (`answer_held`; the wait's `answer`, `note`, `answered_at`) and the spec stays `awaiting_you`. When the turn is free, answered parked specs go first, oldest `answered_at` first, before the next queued spec: only then is the `signal` input written (and, for a `needs-you` park the worker ended by going busy, `unparked`). Under `engine run`, where no other spec exists, an answer is applied in the tick that drains it, as in part 1.
- The answer's `ruling` event and `ask` metrics line (Task 4) are written when the answer is applied, with the stored `answered_at`.
- A running job whose spec is `awaiting_you` does not block another spec's dispatch (assumption A3); its status events are still drained and its job end still recorded, but no job, check or integrate step of a spec without the turn is started.
- End of the queue: when no spec holds the turn, none is queued, no parked spec has an answer waiting, no lead turn is open and the inbox has no new row, every `awaiting_you` spec without an outcome gets `parked_failed` (outcome `failed — awaiting you: <question>`; state, wait, worktree and windows untouched; `metrics record … --outcome failed` as step `metrics_record:<spec>:parked` when it has a batch). Then the report hook runs (`opts.report`, a no-op until Task 9), `queue_finished {report}` is written, and `engine start` exits 0.
- `engine resume` uses the same loop: a spec in `awaiting_you` with an outcome and a new answer is resumed, runs to its real outcome and is recorded again by `finalize` (step `metrics_record:<spec>`). A queue that already has `queue_finished` and no spec enqueued after it writes no second report and no second `queue_finished`; the loop exits when nothing is runnable. `engine resume` no longer waits forever on an unanswered parked spec.
- Section 9 order on every start: intent steps, due timers, inbox, policy, then running jobs.

**Files:**
- Create: `engine/test/engine_queue_parking.test.js`
- Modify: `engine/lib/engine/core.js`, `engine/lib/engine/queue.js`, `engine/lib/engine/cli.js`, `engine/test/engine_queue.test.js`, `engine/test/engine_resume.test.js`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Spec Testing, "Parking across the queue": a three-spec queue whose first spec parks on a user gate. The second runs; `engine signal <first> approve` written while the second runs yields `answer_held` and no state change; when the second is done the first resumes and finishes before the third's `spec_started` (by seq).
- [ ] The same queue with no answer: at the end the first spec is `awaiting_you` with outcome `failed — awaiting you: user gate: …`, its wait still open, one `metrics record … --outcome failed` call in the stub's log, a `queue_finished` event, and `engine start` exits 0. Then `engine signal <first> approve` and `engine resume`: the spec ends `done` with `kept …`, a second `metrics record` call carries that outcome, and there is still exactly one `queue_finished` event.
- [ ] Two parked specs answered in the reverse of their parking order resume in the order of their answers.
- [ ] A spec parked on `needs-you`: the next spec's job is dispatched while the first spec's job row is still `running`; when the scripted worker of the first goes busy and later writes its report, its job is recorded done and no further job of the first spec is created or dispatched until the second spec is done.
- [ ] `engine resume` with one answered and one unanswered parked spec finishes the answered one and exits; a test fails if it runs longer than 30 s.
- [ ] Aged state: one in-process run with an injected clock parks a spec on `needs-you`, ends the queue, and answers 26 hours later, across a day boundary, with three workers' jobs in the database: the deadline timers that came due in between fire once each and do not fail the parked job, and the spec then runs to its outcome.
- [ ] Kill at each distinct event kind of the three-spec parking run (kill points read from one uninterrupted run, as part 1's resume suite does), then `engine start`: the same final outcomes and the same order of `spec_started`, `signal`, `spec_done`, `fail_spec`, `parked_failed` and `queue_finished` events; `engine rebuild --check` exits 0. Each iteration appends `<kill point> <ok|FAIL> <ms>` to a tally printed on failure.
- [ ] Budget, spec 8b last bullet, across the queue: a spec that parks on its cap gives the turn away like any other park.
- [ ] Guard tests name their mutations (at least: "apply an answer as soon as it is drained" → the answer-during-the-second test fails; "skip the outcome check at idle" → a second `queue_finished`).

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `queue_report.render({db, project, outputs}) -> text` is pure (no I/O but the database reads). The text has, in this order: `# Queue report <YYYY-MM-DD>`; the line `Written by the engine (<project>).`; `## Specs` with one `### <spec id>` per spec in queue order holding `- Outcome:`, `- Runner:`, `- Branch:` (plus `- Merge commit:` or `- MR:` when the events have one), for an engine-run spec `- Spend: attempts a/A · tokens t/T` (with ` (lower bound)` by Task 5's rule), `- Rulings:` (each `ruling` event as `<text> — cost if wrong: <cost>`, or `none`; for a lead-run spec the one line `(lead-run: the lead appends its rulings)`), `- Permission prompts seen:` (the `needs_you` events' windows, or `none`), `- User gates waiting:` (open `user_gate` waits, or `none`); `## Awaiting you` (per parked spec: the `I recommend: …` line, the question, and `tmux-ctl engine signal <spec> <options>`; or `none`); `## Metrics` (the `metrics report` output per batch, then `Analysis: <path>` for each path `registry report` printed, then the `metrics status` line, which starts `PCEE:` in this repo); `## Sleep` (the `awake sleeps` lines, or `none`).
- [ ] The date is the UTC date of the queue's first `spec_added` event. Aged fixture: a database whose queue starts at 23:50 UTC and finishes at 00:20 the next day, with two specs, one parked, and jobs from three workers; the report is named for the start date and lists both specs in queue order.
- [ ] `queue_report.write(ctx)` runs, each as a step that never blocks (Global Constraints): `tmux-ctl registry report <batch>` and `tmux-ctl metrics report <batch>` per distinct batch, `tmux-ctl metrics status`, `tmux-ctl awake sleeps <ISO time of the first spec_added>`; writes the file under the main checkout (`<date>-queue.md`, or `<date>-queue-2.md` and so on when that name exists and its second line is not this project's `Written by the engine` line from this queue); commits it with `docs/superpowers/metrics/runs.jsonl`, `docs/superpowers/metrics/tasks.jsonl` and the analysis paths, path-scoped, as `docs(report): queue <date>` with the trailer `Engine-Step: commit_report:<file>` (step kind `commit_report`), only when `integrate.liveCheckoutBusy` answers null and the main checkout is on `main`, else writes one `report_uncommitted {reason}` event; then `tmux-ctl artifact <path>` and `tmux-ctl awake off`. - [ ] Task 8's end-to-end queue tests now find the report file and `[Engine] queue finished: docs/superpowers/reports/<date>-queue.md` in the lead-lines file.
